LESSON: PLANT GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Life Science
Topic 1.6: Plant growth and development
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Plant growth and development, part of Life Science in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: Why is the concept of growth in plants important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use digital or print media to search for differences between growth and development in plants. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or adapted digital devices to conduct research. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use digital or print media to search for differences between growth and development in plants. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or adapted digital devices to conduct research. Regulate screen resolution appropriately for learners who are sensitive to light,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Plant growth and development together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: as the learner shares information gathered on differences between plant growth and

development.

● Self-efficacy: as the learner works on practical activities to investigate epigeal and hypogeal germination.

● Learning to learn: as the learner reflects on the experiments investigating conditions necessary for germination.

Values:
● Respect: as the learner discusses with peers the differences between primary and secondary growth in plants.

● Responsibility: as the learner engages in assigned roles while working with others in the process of learning such as

investigating conditions necessary for germination.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Cyber security: as the learner observes online security when searching for information on growth and development of plants.
